title: Paraneoplastic Limbic Encephalitis in a Male with Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Lung
case_prompt:
A 54-year-old Caucasian man with a 20–pack-year smoking history and no prior medical problems was admitted for subacute onset of neurologic symptoms. Over several weeks he developed nocturnal myoclonus, sexual dysfunction, mood swings, insomnia, daytime sleepiness, and occasional disorientation. Vital signs were normal, and general physical examination was unremarkable. Neurologic examination showed anterograde amnesia, apathy, and a Mini-Mental State Examination score of 24/30.

Laboratory studies revealed normal complete blood count and metabolic panel. Serologic tests were negative for hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus, human immunodeficiency virus, leishmaniasis, histoplasmosis, syphilis, and borreliosis. Immunologic studies showed normal results for antinuclear antibodies, anti–double-stranded DNA antibody, angiotensin-converting enzyme, complement levels, IgA, antineutrophil cytoplasmic autoantibodies, anti-Ro/La antibody, and anticardiolipin antibody; serum protein electrophoresis was normal. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed no malignant cells, and polymerase chain–reaction testing was negative for herpes simplex virus and varicella zoster virus. Paraneoplastic antibody testing in the CSF was negative for antibodies against Hu, Yo, Ri, Ta, amphiphysin, and Ma2 antigens. The electroencephalogram was normal.

Noncontrast cranial CT demonstrated hypodense lesions in the medial bitemporal regions and right caudate nucleus, with pseudonodular uptake in both unci. Brain MRI FLAIR sequences revealed diffuse hyperintensities predominantly in the medial temporal lobes, extending into the basal ganglia, frontal lobes, and leptomeninges, suggesting a limbic encephalitis.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Metabolic and toxic encephalopathy unlikely — “All blood test findings were within normal limits…”  
2. Systemic infections excluded — “Serology was negative for hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus, human immunodeficiency virus, leishmaniasis, histoplasmosis, syphilis, and borreliosis.”  
3. Viral encephalitis excluded — “A polymerase chain reaction performed using the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) yielded negative findings for herpes simplex and varicella zoster virus.”  
4. Autoimmune encephalitis excluded — “The findings of immunological studies were normal for antinuclear antibodies, anti-DNA antibody, angiotensin-converting enzyme, complement, IgA, antineutrophil cytoplasmic autoantibodies, anti-Ro/La antibody, and anticardiolipin antibody; a proteinogram also yielded normal findings.”  
5. CNS neoplasm (primary or metastatic) less likely — “A cytologic analysis of the CSF did not reveal any malignant cells.”  
6. Paraneoplastic limbic encephalitis supported by imaging — “MRI demonstrated diffuse hyperintensities in the parenchyma, with predominantly medial bitemporal involvement extending into the basal ganglia, frontal lobes, and leptomeninges on FLAIR images… suggesting a PLE.”
